newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil central bank still to run state banks.
newsitem.headline: Brazil central bank still to run state banks.

text.p: A decree on the restructuring of state banks re-issued on Thursday allowed Brazil's Central Bank to extend for 180 days the management of state banks Banerj and Banespa, a Central Bank spokesman said.
"The new version of the decree grants the Central Bank the possibility of extending for six months its management of Banerj and Banespa," he said.
However, the spokesman said the Central Bank has not decided yet whether it will extend its administration of the two state banks.
The Central Bank took over Banerj and Banespa in December 1994 to initially run the two banks for one year but its management was extended for 12 more months.
The Central Bank's administration would expire on December 27 this year and could not be extended again unless a government decree was issued.
Regarding Banerj, the government decree gives the Rio de Janeiro state government more time to sell the bank if it is not eventually privatized this year.
Rio officials on Thursday said Banerj will go on sale on December 26 after the state succeeded in lifting a court injunction that blocked the selloff last Tuesday.
The two investors who signed up for the auction -- Banco Itau and Bradesco -- will have to present financial guarantees on Monday to bid on the auction.
